item.title: A single liver-sparing myotropic AAV ameliorates muscular dystrophy in humanized mice by base editing.
item.abstract: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is caused by mutations in the DMD gene, most of which are large exon deletions that result in loss of dystrophin protein. Adenine base editing (ABE) enables permanent gene correction by modifying splice sites to cause exon skipping and restoration of the DMD open reading frame. We previously demonstrated that adeno-associated virus 9-mediated (AAV9-mediated) delivery of adenine base editors allows efficient gene editing in mouse models of DMD. However, conventional AAV-based gene delivery approaches are complicated by their limited packaging capacity and high-dose-related toxicity. Here, we describe a single AAV vector encoding a compact adenine base editor, SlugABE8e, and a single-guide RNA, which enable efficient editing in a humanized DMD mouse model at a lower dose using the muscle-tropic MyoAAV4 capsid. Systemic MyoAAV4A delivery in juvenile DMD mice efficiently restored dystrophin expression in the heart and skeletal muscles. This molecular rescue was accompanied by reduced serum creatine kinase activity and diminished muscle pathology. A liver-detargeted MyoAAV4E-off capsid eliminated viral entry and editing in the liver. We also explored a high-fidelity base editor, SlugHF-ABE8e(V106W), which showed similar on-target and off-target editing to SlugABE8e. Together, these findings establish an all-in-one AAV strategy that efficiently mitigates DMD disease progression.

item.title: Protocol for comprehensive genotyping of nuclease, base, and prime editing outcomes using CleanFinder.
item.abstract: Genome editing experiments often produce heterogeneous allele mixtures that require structured genotyping. Here, we present a protocol for analyzing amplicon sequencing data from nuclease, base, prime, and mitochondrial base editing experiments using CleanFinder. We describe steps for preparing reference sequences and FASTQ files and running browser-native or command-line analyses. We then detail interpretation of genotype distributions, repair signatures, editing efficiencies, and allelic dropout. For complete details on the use and execution of this protocol, please refer to Ramachandran et al.1 and cleanfinder.org.

item.title: Rational design of L-Pantolactone dehydrogenase to enhance the activity of whole-cell biocatalyst.
item.abstract: L-Pantolactone dehydrogenase (LPLDH) is a key biocatalyst for the production of the chiral pharmaceutical intermediate D-pantolactone (D-PL). To address the limitations of low whole-cell catalytic activity and poor industrial applicability in the wild-type (WT) AmeLPLDH from Amycolatopsis methanolica, we employed a combined strategy of rational design and directed evolution. Using AlphaFold2-predicted structures, molecular docking, and bioinformatic analysis, residue T271 was identified as a critical functional determinant. Among the constructed variants, the T271D mutant exhibited a significant increase in whole-cell catalytic activity, with an 8.2-fold higher conversion rate than the wild type. Subsequent 50-ns molecular dynamics simulations suggested that the T271D mutation may rigidify the surface loop (residues 163-177). CD spectroscopy further showed that the overall secondary structure was largely preserved, with local secondary-structure changes consistent with this hypothesis. These findings are consistent with, but do not directly prove, a loop-rigidification mechanism. This study identifies a promising variant for further development, providing a basis for the practical application of AmeLPLDH and providing an improved biocatalyst for the green synthesis of D-pantolactone.

item.title: Expression and purification of SP6 RNA polymerase for in vitro transcription.
item.abstract: Construction of a plasmid for efficient overexpression of SP6 RNA polymerase in E. coli and method of purification of multi-milligram quantities of this enzyme by two chromatographic steps is described. SP6 RNA polymerase purified by this method is highly active and stable in described storage conditions at -20 °C for many years. Due to its specific 5' sequence (5'-GAATACA…) uncapped mRNA synthesized by SP6 RNA polymerase can be used for cell-free translation yielding several times more protein product than uncapped mRNAs produced by other polymerases. These factors greatly reduce the costs of in vitro production of mRNA for cell-free translation, improving the feasibility of this protein expression system for various applications.

item.title: The Alzheimer's disease-associated rs28834970 variant in PTK2B impairs electrical activity and regulates Tau phosphorylation and APP processing in human neuronal cultures
item.abstract: Background: Genome-wide association studies have identified the PTK2B gene, which encodes Proline-rich tyrosine kinase 2 (PYK2), as a genetic risk factor for Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, its role in AD aetiology remains to be understood, as a complex contribution to amyloid {beta} (A{beta}) toxicity, tauopathy and neuronal dysfunction is suggested by contradictory evidence. Determining how the causal variant among AD-associated PTK2B variants impairs PYK2 function to trigger AD hallmarks could bring clarification. Methods: We combined in silico prediction tools with luciferase reporter assays in neuroblastoma cells to prioritize potential AD-associated PTK2B functional variants. We generated isogenic KOLF2.1J induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) carrying the most relevant functional variant using CRISPR-Cas9 and differentiated them into human neuronal cultures (hNCs). We assessed PYK2 expression via immunoblotting, performed transcriptomic profiling using RNA-sequencing, analyzed neuronal network activity via multielectrode array (MEA) recordings, quantified synaptic density through immunocytochemistry in microfluidic devices, and assessed Tau phosphorylation and amyloid-precursor protein (APP) metabolism. Results: The rs28834970 regulatory variant was identified as the most functionally relevant in our model, with the C risk allele promoting transcription factor C/EBP{beta} binding within a cis-regulatory element. In hNCs, the homozygous rs28834970 CC genotype reduced total PYK2 levels by more than 80%, while increasing the proportion of phosphorylated (activated) PYK2. Transcriptomic analysis revealed 724 downregulated and 113 upregulated gene sets, with altered expression of genes involved in extracellular matrix organization, cytoplasmic translation and neurotransmitter secretion. MEA recordings showed reduced network recruitment and altered burst organization. Immunocytochemistry in microfluidic devices consistently revealed that rs28834970 impacts dendritic development and postsynaptic maturation. The risk genotype significantly elevated Tau phosphorylation at pathological sites (Thr181, Thr217, Thr231, Ser202-Thr205, Ser396-Ser404), and enhanced APP processing, resulting in decreased levels of APP and CTF but increased levels of sAPP, sAPP{beta} and A{beta}. Conclusion: The rs28834970 C risk allele mechanistically links AD susceptibility to downregulation of PTK2B/PYK2 expression and to the increase in Tau pathology and A{beta} levels while compromising synaptic structure and function.
item.authors: Lannette-Weimann, N.,  Huyvaert, M.,  Limoge, F.,  Lemaire, M.,  Gao, V.,  Mauri

item.title: Mg2+ deficiency affects heat shock resistance in Escherichia coli.
item.abstract: While thermal processing remains central to ensuring food safety, sublethal heat intensities stemming from gradients or from milder processing efforts risk enabling microbial adaptation. In efforts to investigate the capacity of foodborne bacteria to acquire heat resistance, most studies have focused on stationary phase cells, although many regions of the food processing chain are permissive for growth. To determine how growth-competent cells can adapt to heat through evolution, we subjected exponentially growing Escherichia coli MG1655 cells to iterative heat cycling. Interestingly, while all evolved lineages readily acquired improved heat shock resistance, none of them seemed to do so via the anticipated upregulation of heat shock proteins. In contrast, whole genome sequencing indicated that most lineages acquired loss-of-function mutations in mgrB, encoding a negative regulator of the PhoPQ two-component signal transduction system. Further genetic analysis revealed that upregulation of the PhoPQ-dependent MgtA Mg2+ importer was causal for the heat shock resistance. Moreover, chemical Mg2+ supplementation phenocopied this resistance and even improved heat survival of several pathogenic enterobacteria. Our findings highlight cellular Mg2+ homeostasis as a key determinant of intrinsic heat resistance in several proliferating enterobacteria, and underscore how both adaptive mutations and Mg2+ availability can readily impose increased heat resistance in the food processing chain.

item.title: Epigenetic targeting of an HBO1-H3K9la-CHI3L1 axis reduces regulatory B cell-mediated CD8+ T cell dysfunction in lung adenocarcinoma.
item.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aberrant glycolysis and lactate accumulation are hallmarks of solid tumors, yet how tumor-derived lactate contributes to tumor progression has not been fully defined. This study intends to examine the role of glycolysis in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) growth and immunosuppression, and to explore the underpinning mechanisms.
METHODS: Syngeneic Lewis lung carcinoma models and autochthonous KrasLSL-G12D LUAD mice were used. Glycolysis was inhibited by 2-DG or LDH knockdown, followed by tumor growth and immune-cell composition assessments. Therapeutic anti-IL-35 blockade and CD8+ T depletion were performed using neutralizing antibodies. Chitinase 3-like 1 (CHI3L1) expression, regulatory B cell (Breg) polarization, and B-cell-mediated T-cell suppression were assessed by flow cytometry, RNA sequencing, qPCR, ELISA, immunohistochemistry, and co-culture assays. CUT&Tag, chromatin immunoprecipitation, co-immunoprecipitation, and cell-free transferase assays were used to define the lactylation mechanism.
RESULTS: Glycolysis restriction suppressed tumor growth and metastatic colonization, reduced CD1dhiCD5+IL-35+ Bregs, and restored GZMB+CD8+ T cells. CHI3L1 was markedly downregulated after glycolysis inhibition, whereas recombinant CHI3L1 restored IL-13Rα2+ Breg polarization and impaired CD8+ T-cell responses through STAT3 activation. Lactate increased H3K9 lactylation and CHI3L1 expression, while glycolysis inhibition reduced H3K9la enrichment at the Chi3l1 promoter. HBO1 directly catalyzed H3K9 lactylation and promoted CHI3L1 production. Genetic or pharmacological HBO1 blockade reduced Bregs, enhanced cytotoxic T-cell activity, and improved the efficacy of anti-PD-1 therapy.
CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates the participation of an HBO1-H3K9la-CHI3L1–IL-13Rα2-STAT3 axis in tumor glycolysis-established Breg polarization and CD8+ T dysfunction. Targeting HBO1 may provide a strategy to enhance the efficacy of PD-1 blockade in LUAD.

item.title: TaMYB39 positively regulates salt tolerance in wheat seedlings.
item.abstract: Salt stress severely restricts wheat growth and productivity, yet the regulatory mechanisms governing the abundance and activity of stress-responsive transcription factors remain incompletely understood. In this study, we characterized the wheat MYB transcription factor TaMYB39 and investigated its role in salt tolerance and protein stability. TaMYB39 expression was rapidly induced by NaCl treatment, and the protein was predominantly localized in the nucleus. Transgenic wheat lines overexpressing TaMYB39 exhibited improved growth and greater dry weight under salt stress, whereas RNAi lines showed increased sensitivity. TaMYB39 overexpression was associated with reduced Na⁺ accumulation, enhanced K⁺ retention, a lower Na⁺/K⁺ ratio, increased proline accumulation, and reduced membrane damage. The overexpression lines also accumulated less H2O2 and O2- and exhibited higher SOD, POD, and CAT activities, consistent with enhanced antioxidant capacity. Yeast two-hybrid screening identified the bZIP transcription factor TabZIP27 as a TaMYB39-interacting protein, and this interaction was confirmed by pairwise Y2H, BiFC, GST pull-down, and Co-IP assays. Salt treatment enhanced the TaMYB39-TabZIP27 interaction. Cell-free degradation and CHX chase assays further showed that TabZIP27 delayed TaMYB39 degradation, whereas MG132 treatment attenuated the decline in TaMYB39 abundance, supporting the involvement of the 26S proteasome pathway in TaMYB39 turnover. Collectively, these findings identify TaMYB39 as a positive regulator of salt tolerance in wheat and suggest that its protein stability is modulated through interaction with TabZIP27 under salt stress.

item.title: Prognostic Significance of Early Donor-derived Cell-free DNA Trajectories After Kidney Transplantation.
item.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early post-transplant elevations in donor-derived cell-free DNA are often attributed to ischemia-reperfusion injury, with uncertain prognostic significance. We assessed whether donor-derived cell-free DNA (dd-cfDNA) results during the first 4 mo post-transplantation are associated with long-term graft outcomes.
METHODS: We analyzed 1137 kidney transplant recipients enrolled in the prospective multicenter Kidney Outcomes AlloSure Registry. Recipients were categorized into 4 trajectory groups based on dd-cfDNA measurements obtained within the first 4 mo post-transplant: consistently low, transient-elevation, late-elevation, and persistent-elevation. Associations with donor-specific antibody (DSA) development, rejection, graft dysfunction, and graft loss were evaluated over 3 y using hazard regression, with multivariable models adjusted for calculated Panel Reactive Antibody (cPRA) and retransplant.
RESULTS: Among the 1137 recipients, 83.7% exhibited consistently low dd-cfDNA, 9.8% transient-elevation, 3.2% late-elevation, and 3.3% persistent-elevation. Late elevation was associated with the highest cumulative incidence of DSA development, whereas persistent-elevation had the highest incidence of rejection, graft dysfunction, and graft loss. Graft loss occurred in 20.0% of recipients with persistent-elevation and 8.8% with late-elevation and was uncommon among consistently low (2.2%) and transient (2.9%) groups. On multivariable analysis, late elevation was independently associated with DSA development, rejection, and graft loss, and persistent-elevation with rejection, graft dysfunction, and graft loss, regardless of prior transplantation or sensitization status.
CONCLUSIONS: Early dd-cfDNA trajectories stratify kidney transplant recipients into clinically meaningful risk phenotypes. Persistent or late-emerging elevation identifies patients at independently increased risk of rejection and graft loss, with persistent-elevation also associated with graft dysfunction, supporting serial dd-cfDNA monitoring as a tool for early post-transplant risk stratification.

item.title: Gαi3 acts as a metabolic checkpoint orchestrating TAMs immunosuppression and lipid metabolism in glucose-deprived hepatocellular carcinoma.
item.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are abundant in the hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) tumor microenvironment (TME) and undergo metabolic reprogramming to support an immunosuppressive phenotype. While G protein-coupled receptors are known sensors of environmental cues, the specific role of the inhibitory G protein subunit alpha i3 (Gαi3) in linking metabolic stress to TAMs-mediated immunosuppression remains undefined.
METHODS: Clinical associations were evaluated by multiplex immunohistochemistry, Kaplan-Meier analysis, and multivariable Cox regression. Myeloid-specific Gnai3-deficient mice were studied in DEN/CCl4 or DEN/HFD-induced and orthotopic HCC models. Metabolic reprogramming was assessed by targeted metabolomics, Seahorse analysis, and pharmacological inhibition of fatty acid oxidation. Mechanistic studies included co-immunoprecipitation, a cell-free kinase assay using recombinant AMPK and Gαi3, chromatin immunoprecipitation, promoter-reporter assays, cycloheximide-chase analysis, surface-biotinylation-based EGFR recycling assays, and GBF1 knockdown/rescue experiments.
RESULTS: Gαi3 was upregulated in TAMs within glucose-deprived HCC regions and was associated with M2-like polarization, CD8+T cell exhaustion, and shorter overall survival. High TAM Gαi3 remained associated with overall survival after adjustment for clinical covariates. Myeloid-specific Gnai3 deletion suppressed HCC progression and restored cytotoxic CD8+T cell activity. Etomoxir phenocopied Gnai3 deficiency and attenuated macrophage-mediated T-cell suppression, supporting a requirement for fatty acid oxidation. Mechanistically, glucose deprivation activated AMPK-dependent phosphorylation of Gαi3; the cell-free kinase assay, mass spectrometry, and S143A mutagenesis together supported Ser143 as the relevant regulatory site. Active Gαi3 stabilized EGFR through a GBF1-associated trafficking program, promoted EGFR-dependent PKM2 nuclear translocation, and enhanced formation of a nuclear PKM2/HIF-1α transcriptional complex that activated Pparg and sustained an immunosuppressive fatty acid oxidation program.
CONCLUSIONS: Our study identifies Gαi3 as a critical metabolic checkpoint that orchestrates TAMs immunosuppression in the glucose-deprived TME. The Gαi3-EGFR-PKM2-PPARγ signaling axis drives metabolic reprogramming towards lipid oxidation, thereby inhibiting antitumor immunity. Targeting Gαi3 represents a novel immunotherapeutic strategy to reverse TAMs-mediated immunosuppression and improve outcomes in HCC.

item.title: Accuracy of plasma cell-free DNA PCR versus mNGS for non-invasive diagnosis of invasive mold disease.
item.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) detection in plasma is a novel testing modality for non-invasive diagnosis of invasive mold disease (IMD) in immunocompromised patients. The accuracy of PCR compared to metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) for diagnosis of IMD remains unknown. Plasma samples from patients with proven and probable IMD and no IMD were tested with mold PCR and shotgun mNGS. Mold PCR detected Aspergillus species, Mucorales agents, Fusarium species, Scedosporium species, and Lomentospora prolificans. The sensitivity and specificity of mold PCR and mNGS were measured. Ninety-four patients with proven (48) and probable (48) IMD due to Aspergillus species (64), Mucorales agents (13), Scedosporium species and Lomentospora prolificans (13), and Fusarium species (6), and 62 patients with no IMD were included in this study. 99.4% (155) of the patients were immunosuppressed. The overall sensitivity and specificity were 62.5% (60/96; 95% CI 52.0-72.2) and 99.8% (535/536; 95% CI 99.0-100), respectively, for mold PCR and 43.8% (42/96; 95% CI 33.6-54.3; P < 0.001) and 99.6% (534/536; 95% CI 98.7-100; P = 1.0), respectively, for mNGS. The proportion of mold PCR-positive mNGS-negative results was 16.0% (4/25) in focal cases compared with 25.0% (11/44; P = 0.384) and 18.5% (5/27; P = 0.810) in multifocal and disseminated cases, respectively. The median PCR cycle threshold was 40.6 (IQR, 37.5-41.5) in PCR-positive mNGS-negative cases compared with 37.3 (IQR, 34.5-39.3; P = 0.004) in PCR-positive mNGS-positive cases. Plasma cfDNA PCR is more sensitive than mNGS for the diagnosis of IMD in immunocompromised patients. Lower sensitivity of mNGS was associated with lower mold cfDNA burden.
IMPORTANCE: Invasive mold disease (IMD) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in immunocompromised patients. Early diagnosis and initiation of tailored antifungal therapy are critical for optimizing outcomes in patients with IMD. Detection of circulating fungal cell-free DNA (cfDNA) in the acellular fraction of blood is a novel testing modality that is increasingly used for early and non-invasive diagnosis of IMD. This study represents the first head-to-head accuracy study to compare the sensitivity and specificity of PCR with mNGS for the diagnosis of IMD. The study showed that the overall mold PCR was significantly more sensitive compared with mNGS, while both assays demonstrated very high specificity. Similar trends were observed in a smaller subgroup of patients with invasive aspergillosis, mucormycosis, and scedosporiosis. The findings have implications for assay selection when seeking to non-invasively diagnose IMD in immunocompromised patients.

item.title: Peripheral molecular signatures of major depressive disorder: a systematic review of blood-derived biomarkers for diagnosis, stratification, and treatment response.
item.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is biologically heterogeneous, yet diagnosis and treatment selection remain largely symptom-based. Blood-derived molecular biomarkers may offer scalable tools for biomarker discovery, biological stratification, and treatment-response research, but their clinical readiness remains uncertain.
METHODS: This PRISMA-compliant systematic review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261379864). PubMed, Scopus, and Embase were searched from 2014 to 27 April 2026 for human studies evaluating blood-derived molecular biomarkers in MDD or clinically defined depressive phenotypes with extractable depression-relevant data. Eligible domains included transcriptomics, DNA methylation, non-coding RNA, immune-inflammatory, mitochondrial/metabolic, neurotrophic/neuroendocrine, multi-omics, and machine-learning biomarker studies. Owing to methodological and platform heterogeneity, a structured narrative synthesis was performed rather than quantitative meta-analysis. Methodological quality was assessed using a modified QUADOMICS framework, prediction-model studies were additionally assessed using PROBAST, and certainty was judged using a modified GRADE approach.
RESULTS: Of 9,354 records identified, 25 reports met the eligibility criteria, representing 24 independent participant datasets because two methylation analyses used the same underlying NESDA cohort. Included studies used whole blood, PBMCs, leukocytes, monocytes, serum, plasma, and cell-free RNA across diverse molecular platforms. Individual biomarkers were heterogeneous, but recurrent pathway-level signals involved immune-inflammatory and interferon-related pathways, NF-κB signalling, mitochondrial and energy metabolism, DNA methylation and epigenetic regulation, neurodevelopmental/synaptic pathways, stress-response signalling, autophagy, and non-coding RNA regulation. Multi-marker and multi-omics panels showed promising apparent diagnostic or treatment-response relevance, but most were internally validated, cohort-specific, or exploratory. Modified GRADE certainty was low to very low across biomarker domains.
CONCLUSIONS: Blood-derived molecular signatures in MDD show stronger convergence at the pathway level than at the individual-biomarker level. Current evidence supports hypothesis generation and biological stratification, but no blood-derived biomarker or panel is ready for routine diagnosis or treatment selection.

item.title: Preliminary in vitro evaluation of biological responses associated with an Elumbotti-derived coating on titanium cortical screws.
item.abstract: The biological response to coating-derived components is an important consideration in the preliminary development of functionalized titanium implants. In the present study, an Elumbotti (Ormocarpum cochinchinense)-derived composite coating was applied to titanium cortical screws (12 mm), and its preliminary in vitro biological response was investigated using a cell-free protein-denaturation assay and MG-63 osteoblast-like cells. Uncoated titanium (T1) and Elumbotti-coated titanium cortical screw samples (ST1) were included in the experimental evaluation. Bovine serum albumin (BSA) protein-denaturation inhibition was assessed as a preliminary cell-free measure of protein-stabilizing activity, with diclofenac sodium used as the reference standard. MG-63 cellular responses were evaluated using MTT viability, scratch-wound closure, and acridine orange/ethidium bromide (AO/EtBr) fluorescence staining assays. The MTT assay evaluated concentration-dependent responses to the ST1 test preparation, whereas the scratch-wound and AO/EtBr assays evaluated cellular responses following exposure to conditioned medium obtained from ST1-coated titanium cortical screws. ST1 demonstrated greater BSA protein-denaturation inhibitory activity than T1, with calculated IC50 values of 63.032 and 118.379 µg/mL, respectively. In the MTT assay, MG-63 viability showed a concentration-dependent response to the ST1 test preparation, remaining above 70% at concentrations up to 32 µg/mL and decreasing below 70% at concentrations of 64 µg/mL and above. Scratch-wound closure following exposure to ST1-conditioned medium increased from 67.07% at 24 h to 83.45% at 48 h, compared with 27.24% and 34.50%, respectively, in untreated control cells. AO/EtBr staining demonstrated time-dependent changes in cell viability and membrane integrity following prolonged exposure to ST1-conditioned medium. Overall, the findings provide preliminary evidence of concentration- and time-dependent biological responses associated with the Elumbotti-derived coating system and its soluble components. However, the present assays do not establish direct cell-coating interactions, cellular anti-inflammatory activity, osteogenic differentiation, osseointegration, or improved orthopedic implant performance. Further batch-specific physicochemical characterization, direct cell-surface studies, coating stability and release analyses, osteogenic and inflammatory-marker evaluation, and in vivo investigation are required to establish the biological and functional relevance of the coating for orthopedic applications.

cards.title_cn: 徐州市长期护理保险赋能基层医疗机构新发展
cards.one_liner: 徐州将长护险服务嵌入基层医疗机构，农村失能人员可在家门口获得专业照护。
key_findings: 长护险服务合理嵌入乡镇卫生院等基层医疗机构，盘活闲置病床与医护人力。
重点破解农村失能群体“就医不便、照护不足”难题，提供上门照护。
属地方医保部门落实长护险制度的实践，发布日期为2026-11-02。
cards.why_it_matters: 与合成生物学研发无直接关联，但反映医保支付向基层照护延伸；若涉及居家检测、诊断耗材或数字健康，可关注基层渠道机会。

item.journal: 国家医保局 · 医保动态

cards.score_reason: 机关读书活动，无政策价值
cards.title_cn: 国家医保局举办“书香润初心 医保启新程”读书分享活动
cards.one_liner: 国家医保局举办内部读书分享活动，不涉及医保政策调整。
key_findings: 活动于10月27日举行，局党组成员、副局长王文君出席。
10名青年干部围绕政治理论、红色经典、人文历史、医保业务分享。
属机关文化建设活动，无政策或监管变化内容。
cards.why_it_matters: 与合成生物学研发、产品注册及医保准入无直接关联，仅反映医保局内部文化建设动态。

item.title: Introducing the Grid Protectors Program
item.abstract: OpenAI’s Grid Protectors Program will work with utilities to help future compute campuses support grid reliability and protect consumer electricity costs.

cards.score_reason: OpenAI算力基建与电网合作
cards.title_cn: OpenAI 推出电网保护者计划
cards.one_liner: OpenAI 启动 Grid Protectors 计划，与公用事业合作，确保未来算力园区不损害电网可靠性与居民电价。
key_findings: OpenAI 将与电力公司合作，使未来算力园区支撑电网可靠性
计划明确以保护消费者电价为约束目标
面向未来大规模算力基础设施的用电规划
cards.why_it_matters: AI 算力扩张正成为电力需求与电价的关键变量；合成生物学同样依赖大规模计算与自动化设施，该模式对深圳生物制造与算力基础设施的用电规划有参考价值。

item.title: Speeding up planning decisions with AI
item.abstract: Google DeepMind and UK government work together to reduce planning assessment times

cards.score_reason: DeepMind政府合作应用落地
cards.title_cn: Google DeepMind 与英国政府合作，用 AI 加速规划审批决策
cards.one_liner: Google DeepMind 与英国政府合作，用 AI 缩短规划评估时间。
key_findings: 合作方为 Google DeepMind 与英国政府，目标是压缩规划评估周期。
应用场景是政府规划审批决策，属于 AI 落地公共行政流程。
原文未披露具体技术方案、试点规模或量化效果数据。
cards.why_it_matters: 对合成生物学读者而言，这提示 AI 正进入监管与审批流程；未来涉及基因编辑、生物制造项目的合规评估可能提速，值得关注监管科技动向。

item.title: LifeVal
item.abstract: Introducing LifeVal, a benchmark measuring how well AI helps people complete everyday tasks, from finding childcare to managing finances and government paperwork.

cards.score_reason: OpenAI日常任务基准发布
cards.title_cn: LifeVal：衡量 AI 协助完成日常事务能力的基准
cards.one_liner: OpenAI 发布 LifeVal 基准，评估 AI 在育儿、理财、政务文书等日常事务中的实际帮助能力。
key_findings: LifeVal 覆盖育儿查找、财务管理、政府文书等真实日常任务场景。
该基准衡量 AI 帮助人们完成日常事务的实际效果，而非单项能力测试。
由 OpenAI News 发布，属于 AI 评测基准类工具。
cards.why_it_matters: 对合成生物学研究者而言，此类基准可帮助判断通用 AI 在文献检索、经费与合规文书等科研事务中的实用价值。

item.title: Claude’s new rules against game cloning won’t stop the AI copying boom
item.abstract: The tsunami of imitators is way bigger than any one model maker can stem.

cards.score_reason: Anthropic游戏克隆政策动态
cards.title_cn: Claude 新规禁止游戏克隆，难挡 AI 复制潮
cards.one_liner: Anthropic 为 Claude 新增反游戏克隆规则，但难遏制 AI 模仿浪潮。
key_findings: Claude 新增使用规则，禁止用其克隆游戏。
文章认为模仿者规模远超单一模型厂商可控范围。
AI 复制现象已成行业趋势，单方限制效果有限。
cards.why_it_matters: 对合成生物学读者而言，这反映 AI 生成与知识产权边界收紧的趋势，可能影响用 LLM 辅助设计、代码生成与数据复用的合规判断。

item.title: Qodo builds context into AI code review with Codex
item.abstract: Qodo brings company knowledge and coding standards into Codex, helping developers catch P0 issues across repositories before opening a pull request.

cards.score_reason: AI代码审查工具常规更新
cards.title_cn: Qodo 将公司知识与编码规范注入 Codex，强化 AI 代码审查
cards.one_liner: Qodo 把企业知识与编码标准接入 Codex，让开发者在提交 PR 前跨仓库发现 P0 级问题。
key_findings: Qodo 将公司内部知识与编码规范注入 Codex，使 AI 代码审查具备企业上下文。
可在打开 PR 前跨多个仓库识别 P0 级严重问题，提前拦截风险。
该能力由 OpenAI News 报道，定位为面向开发者的 AI 代码审查增强。
cards.why_it_matters: 合成生物学研发日益依赖自建软件与数据管线，跨仓库的 AI 审查有助于在提交前发现关键缺陷，降低实验数据与自动化流程的出错风险。

item.title: Coming in 2027: Apple’s $1,000 home robot for FaceTime and switching on lights
item.abstract: Apple robot backed by CEO John Ternus may have hefty price tag and limited uses.

cards.score_reason: 苹果家用机器人弱相关
cards.title_cn: 苹果计划2027年推出1000美元家用机器人，主打FaceTime与智能家居控制
cards.one_liner: 苹果拟2027年发布约1000美元家用机器人，由John Ternus主导，功能限于FaceTime和开关灯。
key_findings: 定价约1000美元，预计2027年上市，由CEO John Ternus支持推进。
核心用途为FaceTime通话与智能家居控制，功能范围有限。
高售价与有限用途可能影响其市场接受度。
cards.why_it_matters: 与合成生物学研究无直接关联，但可作为智能家居与实验室自动化终端的潜在参考，优先级较低。

item.title: The world has a new plan to save nature, but it still needs the money
item.abstract: A new action plan aims to rescue 2030 nature targets as financing remains inadequate.

cards.score_reason: 自然保护议题无关
cards.title_cn: 全球自然保护新行动计划出台，资金缺口仍是关键障碍
cards.one_liner: 新行动计划旨在挽救2030年自然目标，但融资仍不足。
key_findings: 新行动计划聚焦挽救2030年自然目标，应对生物多样性进展滞后。
融资不足被明确列为计划落地的主要制约因素。
报道未披露具体资金规模或新增融资机制细节。
cards.why_it_matters: 生物多样性目标与资金机制会影响合成生物学在生物制造、生物资源获取与监管框架上的长期环境政策环境，值得跟踪。
